findings.evidence: Git paths may contain arbitrary bytes except NUL and '/'. A commit adding src/we\xffird/.gitattributes is classified correctly by scripts/risk_floor.py, which decodes paths with errors='surrogateescape', assigns floor D via the basename rule and exits 3. base_gate.run() (line 36) captures that stdout with text=True, i.e. strict UTF-8 decoding, and run_risk is invoked at line 195 outside any try/except. Observed end to end: unhandled UnicodeDecodeError ('utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xff in position 170), process exit 1, stdout completely empty, traceback on stderr. Reproduced from a clean BASE checkout. Paths that are valid non-ASCII UTF-8 (for example src/n-tilde/.gitattributes) are unaffected and score D normally.
findings.falsification_probe: On an exact BASE built from proposed/ bytes: os.makedirs(REPO/'src'/b'we\xffird'.decode('utf-8','surrogateescape')); write '.gitattributes' inside it; git add --all; git commit; then git checkout --detach BASE and run python3 -I -B -S scripts/base_gate.py --mode evaluate --repo . --base $BASE --head $HEAD with binary (not text) capture. Observe exit 1, empty stdout, UnicodeDecodeError traceback. Control: run scripts/risk_floor.py directly with binary capture and observe exit 3 with a correct floor-D payload, proving the defect is in the gate's capture layer and not in classification.
findings.impact: Fail-closed, so this is NOT a false green: the step exits non-zero under set -euo pipefail and the job fails. The damage is to the evidence contract that the rest of the design depends on. A genuine D-classified policy block becomes indistinguishable from infrastructure flakiness because no structured JSON verdict is emitted, and the failure is attributable only by reading a stderr traceback. This compounds R2AA-025, which already tracks masked checker diagnostics. Reachable by any ordinary contributor PR that adds a file with a non-UTF-8 byte in its path.
findings.minimal_fix: In base_gate.run(), capture bytes instead of text and decode explicitly with errors='surrogateescape' before JSON parsing; and wrap the run_risk call in evaluate() with the existing failure-emission path so a structured FAIL payload is always emitted rather than an unhandled traceback. NOT AUTHORIZED BY THIS REVIEW; recorded as a proposal only.
findings.title: Non-UTF-8 path bytes crash base_gate's checker-output capture, producing an unstructured failure with no JSON verdict

findings.evidence: Policy.classify_path checks basename_rules first and returns immediately, ahead of exact_paths and prefix_rules, matching the declared matching.precedence. The only two basename rules are .gitattributes and .gitmodules, both floor D, the maximum class, so no basename match can currently lower an exact or prefix D.
findings.falsification_probe: Add a hypothetical basename rule {basename: 'risk_floors.json', floor: 'B'} to a scratch copy of the policy and classify policy/risk_floors.json: the basename rule wins and the exact_path D is lowered to B. Confirms precedence direction. Not present in these bytes.
findings.impact: No exploitable path for these exact bytes; verified across all probes. The risk is structural and latent: any future basename rule added with a floor below D would silently take precedence over, and lower, a colliding exact_path or prefix_rule D. The current safety is a property of the rule values, not an enforced invariant.
findings.minimal_fix: Add a Policy.__init__ assertion that no basename rule floor ranks lower than any exact_path or prefix_rule floor it could shadow, so the current correctness becomes intentional and enforced. NOT AUTHORIZED BY THIS REVIEW.
findings.title: Basename-first precedence is safe only because both current basename rules are floor D

findings.evidence: Policy basename matching is exact-string. Git's attribute lookup opens the literal name '.gitattributes' per directory, which is also exact-string on ext4, so the two coincide and all tested variants are inert: .GITATTRIBUTES, .Gitattributes, trailing dot, trailing space, U+200B, U+0131 were each committed and none produced CRLF materialization, with core.ignorecase both false and true. A Unicode NFD variant of a pinned fixture classifies B but is a distinct file on ext4.
findings.falsification_probe: Commit tests/.GITATTRIBUTES containing '* text eol=crlf' plus a payload file; read-tree --reset -u on a case-sensitive filesystem and observe LF preserved (inert), then classify the path and observe floor B. The bypass requires a case-folding filesystem to become live, which the pinned runner excludes.
findings.impact: Containment is platform-conditional rather than intrinsic. On a case-folding or NFD-normalizing filesystem (macOS, Windows) a committed .GITATTRIBUTES could be opened when Git asks for .gitattributes while classifying only B. It currently holds because the workflow pins runs-on: ubuntu-latest, and the disk == BASE blob == pinned SHA check is an independent second fail-closed layer that would catch any resulting byte change.
findings.minimal_fix: State the case-sensitive-runner assumption explicitly in the policy's materialization_semantics block so the dependency is auditable rather than implicit, and keep runs-on pinned. NOT AUTHORIZED BY THIS REVIEW.
findings.title: Basename containment coincides with Git semantics only on a case-sensitive, non-normalizing filesystem

findings.evidence: required_pull_request_reviews sets required_approving_review_count=1 with dismiss_stale_reviews=false, require_last_push_approval=false and require_code_owner_reviews=false. enforce_admins=true and required_status_checks.strict=true are appropriate.

Review-only, not configured, so there is no current exposure.

summary: Independent re-review of the R2-4 materialization V2 frozen candidate over exact bytes. Integrity fully verified: BUNDLE_SHA256 and MANIFEST_SHA256 match, 34/34 REVIEW_MANIFEST entries match on path, sha256 and byte count, the ZIP contains no duplicate, traversal or symlink entries, all 7 proposed object hashes match the frozen manifest and the canonical 27/27 scratch manifest, and the probe evidence is bound to the exact frozen manifest SHA with an acyclic one-way binding chain. All 57 C5 checks executed, 57 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 UNCERTAIN, 0 NOT_EXECUTED. Materialization containment held under every adversarial probe: .gitattributes and .gitmodules are D at arbitrary depth including in directory names containing spaces, newlines, Unicode and non-UTF-8 bytes; symlink 120000, gitlink 160000, type changes and deletions are D; executable-bit changes and new executables are C; renames into the control plane are D; the Git mode space is empirically closed to four canonical values so non-canonical crafted tree modes cannot evade mode_findings; parse_raw_z showed zero fail-open across 30 fuzz cases; merge commits cannot hide a D change; and .git/ path injection is rejected by Git itself. C5-16 was answered by separating mechanism from containment: the nested-CRLF lockout is real and was reproduced by forcing the file into a BASE outside the B gate, where it altered both pinned fixtures and the gate then failed closed with AUTHORITY_DISK_HASH_MISMATCH, while ordinary B entry is blocked at D. R2AA-011 and R2AA-014 were re-tested and hold, including assume-unchanged tamper that leaves git status clean, skip-worktree tamper of the gate itself, authority-root and non-BASE-checkout rejection, and the full strict BASE/HEAD binding contract. One new defect was found: NEW-01, in which a non-UTF-8 path byte crashes base_gate's text=True capture of the checker's stdout, yielding exit 1 with no structured JSON verdict. It is fail-closed and therefore not a false green, but it degrades the structured-evidence contract and compounds R2AA-025, so R2AA-024 is held at PARTIAL rather than RESOLVED. R2AA-022 and R2AA-023 are RESOLVED for these exact bytes and R2AA-016 is reassessed from BLOCKING to PARTIAL because its blocking cause is addressed, while R2AA-017 and R2AA-018 remain PARTIAL. The freeze-before-probes claim is correctly labelled procedural throughout and was not mislabelled as cryptographic in any document. New false-green increment is 0; the total remains 6.
